title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: THE DAY'S LEAD — the twenty-one-day "signage negative" is FALSE. Signage Details announced July 31 that its commercial sign construction dataset passed 60,000 standardized technical details across design, permitting, fabrication, mounting, structural conditions and installation, and is offering API access and nonexclusive data licensing
bullets.summary: Primary fetched; published 2026-07-31. This report has written "the physical sign trade that is Brand 9's business has no MCP layer, no API and no protocol" for twenty-one consecutive days, and the counterexample was five weeks old on the day it was last written. Founder John Nauta, verbatim: "We have created more than a drawing library. We have created an intelligence layer that can help connect sign design with the technical requirements needed for permitting, fabrication and installation." Select-A-Sign generates a project-specific technical section detail in ~60 seconds. Published partner targets read like the gap this report kept calling empty: API access and nonexclusive data licensing, AI-assisted detail selection and drawing generation, automated permit and plan-preparation workflows, fabrication and installation software integrations, industry-specific AI grounding, franchise-wide drawing standardization, white-label applications. Already approved as a Fastsigns Preferred Vendor, so franchise distribution is open.
bullets.how: YES — first YES on the signage pillar in three weeks. Licensing is explicitly NONEXCLUSIVE, so it is equally available to every competitor reading the same trade press; the advantage is in being early, not chosen. It is a data layer whose announced applications (permit workflow automation, technical-detail selection, drawing generation) are exactly what B9 does by hand today, while lennar-atlas and resort-signage-concepts are grounded in nothing but our own experience. And an intelligence layer for the sign trade licensed to CAD vendors, AI developers and franchises competes directly with what PRAGMA sells. Read signagedetails.com and price the licence — supplier, partner or threat — rather than leave it another twenty-one days uncategorized.

bullets.title: THE MCP NULL IS ALSO FALSE — the protocol has not been quiet eight weeks. A new roadmap landed August 22, and one of its five priority areas is progressive discovery, written up as the exact problem a fleet of ~130 skills has
bullets.summary: Primary fetched; published 2026-08-22 by both Lead Maintainers. "MCP has been quiet" checked the specification release page; roadmap, governance and extension work publishes on the blog post feed, never opened here. Verbatim: "Connecting to a server with a hundred tools means the model pays for that entire surface before the user has asked a single question, and tool selection tends to get worse as the list grows. We're starting a progressive discovery effort so a server can offer a small entry point and reveal more of its catalog as the conversation narrows." Other four areas: agentic messaging primitives (server-initiated webhooks and channels so clients aren't left polling; maturing Tasks SEP-2663 into the spec); HTTP-native transport unification extending Streamable HTTP to local servers over stdio; agent identity and enterprise security — "MCP authorization today is built around a person approving access in a browser… more and more of the callers are agents running as cloud workloads with their own identity… or delegating narrower authority to sub-agents" — via DPoP (RFC 9449), Workload Identity Federation and the ID-JAG grant behind Enterprise-Managed Authorization, now stable; and SDK conformance.
bullets.how: YES. Progressive discovery is the vendor-side complement to /doctor and /usage: those say which of our ~130 skills are dead weight, progressive discovery changes whether a live one costs anything until needed. The agent-identity area is the more urgent read for a fleet where Hermes holds the only credentialed deploy path — "a person approving access in a browser" is exactly how our credentials work, and the protocol is openly saying that model does not survive sub-agents delegating authority.

bullets.title: HELD ON A SECOND INDEPENDENT READ, AND DATE FAILURE #9 CAUGHT IN A FIFTH DISGUISE — the changelog is identical eight hours later (2.1.263 still one line, 2.1.262 still absent), but a third-party aggregator returned 2.1.259's body under the September 6 heading
bullets.summary: Re-fetched 14:02 ET and parsed for Update label headings. Newest still 2.1.263 / September 6, body still the single bullet "Bug fixes and reliability improvements"; page still jumps to 2.1.261 / September 4 with no 2.1.262. The morning read holds. The near-miss: a search for the September 6 changelog returned a confident, detailed, plausible fix list — claude --bg from a just-deleted directory leaving a crashed session row, Foundry Entra ID upstreams not starting when ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY is set, /schedule routines saved without a message role — presented as the day's release. Every item is real. Every item is from 2.1.259, September 2, four versions earlier, located verbatim at lines 221, 224 and 226 of the fetched primary. Without re-reading the primary this report would have published a rich, specific, well-sourced and completely wrong account of a release whose actual content is six words.
bullets.how: MAYBE — nothing to act on in 2.1.263. But this is the ninth instance of the class and the first where the false content was verifiably TRUE TEXT UNDER A FALSE DATE, the hardest variant to catch because nothing reads as invented. The rule sharpens: a third-party aggregator is not a stale primary, it is a REORDERED one, and the only defence is parsing the primary's own version headings rather than reading its prose.

bullets.title: THE READING QUEUE, NARROWED FROM ARCHITECTURE TO MEASUREMENT — three tool-selection papers that turn "we have too many skills" into a number, one empirically grounded on Claude
bullets.summary: All out of window; named because bullet 2's progressive-discovery effort and this morning's /doctor action both need something to measure against. 2608.04719, 'Diagnosing Tool-Selection Reasoning in LLM Agents with Canary Tools' (5 Aug 2026, Anand & Chattaraj) — abstract read directly. Plants engineered decoy tools in an agent's MCP tool set under a six-type taxonomy: semantic decoys, parameter traps, capability mirages, prerequisite blindness, temporal decoys, granularity traps. 8,640 runs across eight models plus a 2,880-run ablation, dual judges at Cohen's kappa 0.75. Susceptibility ranges ~36x across models, lowest for Claude Opus 4.8; capability tier alone does not predict safety — the most susceptible hosted model is mid-tier and within one provider the cheaper model can be safer; capability mirages are the one type that "most reliably trap frontier models" while the other five are largely inert on strong models. Softening the give-away phrasing left frontier susceptibility unchanged, so the probes measure reasoning not phrase-spotting. Susceptibility predicts task failure at Spearman rho -0.34; framework, schemas, tasks and logs released. Alongside: 2605.24660 (registries from 20 to 3,251 tools) and 2606.16364 ('Looking Is Not Picking').
bullets.how: MAYBE, but the sharpest MAYBE carried here — the canary method is directly runnable and needs no vendor cooperation. Our ~130 skills include several whose descriptions promise more than the skill delivers, which is the definition of a capability mirage, the one decoy class that catches strong models. Order stands: /doctor for the dead-weight count, /usage for attribution, then canaries to test whether the LIVE skills are selected correctly. Architecture papers (2606.20631, 2606.30005) stay behind all three.

bullets.title: NULL SWEEP, NOW STATED WITH ITS QUALIFIER IN FRONT — frontier holds a FOURTH day; agent funding null in window; no new Anthropic first-party item since the 06:02 read. Every one is a null about the surfaces this report checks, and two such nulls were falsified today
bullets.summary: FRONTIER: no model release dated September 4, 5 or 6 from OpenAI, Google, Meta, Mistral, xAI, DeepSeek or Cohere. Newest remain GPT-6 Astra (Sep 3, added to LLM Gateway Sep 4), Gemini 3.8 Flash and Qwen3.8-Max-0902 (Sep 2), Muse Spark 1.3 with contributor tier (Sep 2), Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1 (Sep 1). Early September remains the densest 72 hours of frontier activity this year, and it ended on the 3rd. AGENT FUNDING: nothing material in window; Cognition's $1B+ at $26B was late May, Glean's $150M Series F closed earlier, and Nvidia-Perplexity above $30B is a TALKS story, recorded as unresolved not as news. ANTHROPIC: no new first-party item since this morning (news Sep 1, research Sep 4, Platform Sep 3, Apps Sep 1). Seen in aggregation and explicitly NOT carried: a market-commentary claim of "an October IPO at $800B in play", traceable only to blog commentary; the underlying Google commitment ($10B now at a $350B valuation, up to $30B more on performance targets, 5GW of Google Cloud capacity over five years) is real but dates to April 24, 2026 and is five months out of window.
bullets.how: NO on every market item — with the qualifier now load-bearing rather than decorative. Standing governance gap unchanged and sixteen days old: no rule on training-data-priced model tiers (Meta's muse-spark-1.3-contributor, ~95% cheaper, paid for in prompts and usage patterns). Bullet 4 sharpens rather than softens it — the finding that the cheaper model within a provider can be the SAFER one removes the easy assumption that a discount tier is risky on capability grounds. The risk was never capability. It is what the discount is paid in.

praxis_lesson: Three days, three archive audits, three falsified standing claims — and today's two were both on the pillars this report calls NULL. That is no longer a run of bad luck; it is a structural finding about how this report fails. Its nulls are not observations about the world. They are the shape of its channel list, reported as if they were the shape of the world. "MCP has been quiet eight weeks" meant the specification release page has no new entry — while the protocol's maintainers published a roadmap on the blog feed whose named priority is the precise problem this fleet has. "The sign trade has no API layer, twenty-one days running" meant nothing crossed the searches I ran — while a 60,000-detail permitting-and-fabrication dataset with open nonexclusive API licensing sat five weeks old in the trade press covering Brand 9's own industry. Both nulls were repeated daily with increasing confidence, and repetition was doing the work evidence should have. So the rule that replaces "audit the archive of any new channel" is stronger and costs more: A NULL MUST NAME THE SURFACE IT WAS READ FROM, OR IT MUST NOT BE PUBLISHED. "No MCP news" is not a finding; "no new entry on the MCP specification release page, which is one of four MCP surfaces and not the one carrying roadmap or governance work" is a finding, and it visibly invites the missing check. A null with its surface named is falsifiable in a sentence. A bare null is a claim about everything, defended by nothing, and it hardens every day it is restated. Second, on the day's near-miss: date failure #9 was the most dangerous of the nine, because the content was TRUE — real fixes, accurately described, verbatim from the vendor — and only the date was wrong. Staleness announces itself; reordering does not. A third-party aggregator returning four-day-old release notes under today's heading produces something indistinguishable from good reporting, and the only defence that worked was parsing the primary's own Update label headings rather than reading anyone's prose about them, including the primary's. Third, the two corrections stack into one action rather than two: bullet 2 says the protocol is building progressive discovery because a hundred tools cost the model everything before the first question; bullet 4 says the failure mode surviving on frontier models is the capability mirage, a tool advertising what it cannot do. This fleet has ~130 mostly self-authored skills written over months, several promising more in their description than they deliver. That is not a hypothetical exposure. It is the single documented weakness of strong models, sitting in our own corpus, measurable today with a released framework — and it is a better reason to run /doctor this week than context cost ever was.
